source.publication: 2025 Form 80-100 Resident, Non-Resident and Part-Year Resident Individual Income Tax Instructions (Rev. 12/25) and the 2025 Form 80-105 Resident Return (Rev. 09/25)
source.section: Form 80-105 page 1 lines 8-17 and page 2 lines 38-66; Instructions PDF p.5 Filing Status and Exemptions table; p.6 Additional Exemptions, Lines 8-12; p.7 Lines 14-17; p.22 Tax Rates; p.27 Schedule of Tax Computation lines 1-4; Instructions PDF p.5 Line 3 and Standard Deductions & Exemptions for Married Persons; p.7 Line 15

worked: Federal AGI = wages (person 0) 40,000.00 = 40,000.00. Federal taxable income = 40,000.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction = 24,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Form 80-105 filing status box 3, Married - Filing Separate Returns. Start at federal AGI 40,000.00 (Mississippi builds its own income on lines 38 to 66; the projection starts from federal AGI and takes out the exempt income, the same result here). Line 66 and line 13 Mississippi AGI = 40,000.00. Line 14 standard deduction 2,300.00. Line 8 age boxes checked 0 (taxpayer and spouse each have a box); line 10 = 0 x 1,500.00 = 0.00; line 11 12,000.00; line 12 = 12,000.00; line 15 = one-half of line 12 = 6,000.00 (Line 15, p.7; Line 3, p.5). Line 16 Mississippi taxable income = 40,000.00 - 2,300.00 - 6,000.00 = 31,700.00. Schedule of Tax Computation line 1: first 10,000.00 x 0% = 0.00; line 2: remaining 21,700.00 x 4.4% = 954.80; line 4 and line 17 = 954.80. Lines 18 and 19 credits 0.00; line 20 = 954.80. The form rounds to whole dollars (p.22), which would give 955; expected keeps the formula result. This is one spouse's separate return; the second person is the spouse, under 65, with income on a return of their own.
accepted_approximations: Mississippi builds its own income (Form 80-105 lines 38 to 66); the projection starts from federal AGI and removes the exempt income through the reliefs and Social Security treatment.
